manifesto: The media archive is not a news digest — it is an external audit of the case. Each publication here represents an independent record of facts acknowledged by the professional journalistic community: the contradictions in the Lagovsky case exist, and they are documented.

items.title: Serbia one step from extradition: case passes to the Minister of Justice
items.summary: The Belgrade Court of Appeal confirmed the conditions for extradition on 3 December. The final decision has been referred to the Serbian Minister of Justice — the last instance against whose decision no legal remedy exists. The Radio Slobodna Evropa report documents the transition of the case to its final administrative phase and brings it for the first time into the context of international attention.
items.focus: Defence lawyer Marko Štambuk states plainly that in practice ministers of justice very rarely refuse extradition when courts have established grounds. Publication in RFE — a European media network — means the case has moved beyond the Serbian legal space and become a matter of observation at the regional level.

items.title: N1: Serbian court refused to examine defence evidence — only formal documentation from Moscow
items.summary: The N1 report documents a key procedural contradiction: Lagovsky attempted to present arguments in his defence, but the Court of Appeal stated plainly that it was concerned only with the document received, not with the substance of the charges. Only the formal validity of the request from Moscow was examined. Meanwhile the transaction underlying the charges has been recognised as lawful by arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation — these rulings were not taken into account.
items.focus: Lawyer Štambuk enumerates specific violations: insufficient evidence for a reasonable suspicion — one of the basic requirements for extradition — and the fact that the requesting party has withdrawn from the UN Convention Against Torture and the Council of Europe and is no longer bound by the ECHR. N1 is a CNN-affiliated channel; the publication means procedural violations have been recorded by an independent source.

items.title: Legal deconstruction: how a commercial dispute became a criminal case
items.summary: In 2021, Lagovsky, as an independent lawyer, drafted a land sale agreement between two companies in neither of which he was an employee or owner. The criminal case was opened a year after the transaction — yet the charge was formulated in secret, without notifying the subject, two and a half years later. By that time, arbitration courts up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation had already confirmed the lawfulness of the same transaction.
items.focus: The material is in preparation. Direct quotations from documents and a chronology of key dates will be published upon completion of verification.

press_call.title: For the Press
press_call.text: The entire body of evidence in the case is open and available in full: arbitration rulings up to the Supreme Court of the Russian Federation confirming the lawfulness of the transaction, procedural documents, the defence's position, and primary materials. Journalists may request any documents without restriction.
